letter.subject: Concerns about cookie and tracking practices on convatec.com following rejection of cookies
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive audit of https://convatec.com on 2026-11-08 04:10 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit visited your site, clicked the cookie banner’s “Reject All” option, and recorded what was still stored or sent afterwards.

The points below arise from that audit and from a review of your privacy policy at https://www.convatec.com/cs-cz/zasady-ochrany-osobnich-udaju/.

1. Our review suggests advertising trackers continued after cookies were rejected. Facebook and Google advertising-related requests continued after “Reject All” was clicked, although the policy says users are asked to confirm whether they agree to performance, functional, targeting and social cookies being placed on their device.

2. After rejection, Google still received data: 60 requests were observed to google-analytics.com, googlesyndication.com and googletagmanager.com.

3. After rejection, Facebook still received data: 6 requests were observed to facebook.net.

4. Before any cookie choice was made, two Optimizely cookies were already set: https://www.convatec.com_oeu1794111013047r0.9590165312897165$$21882971979$$session_state and optimizelyEndUserId. These appear to contain a unique identifier.

5. After rejection, 20 requests were observed to optimizely.com.

6. The value of optimizelyEndUserId, which is unique to this browser, was sent to optimizely.com both before any banner choice was made and again after cookies were rejected.

7. We observed Facebook and Optimizely during the audit, but found no mention of them in the privacy policy. The policy may describe them only by category.

8. Our review also suggests the Optimizely cookies and identifier-sharing described above may be difficult to reconcile with the policy statements that only a small number of strictly necessary cookies are placed automatically, and that such information will be disclosed to third-party advertisers or analytics platforms only in the circumstances described there.

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies or trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking that occurs without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
